top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, firm heterogeneity and selection in trade) is the contribution that most changed what economists can ask and measure. It moved the unit of analysis from the industry to the firm, made reallocation a first-order source of gains from openness, and gave firm-level and transaction-level data a theory to be estimated against. It has been checked across many countries for over two decades and has spread into industrial organisation and quantitative macro, so maturity is not a concern. Its main weakness is the credit boundary with Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who are not on the credited list. I judge this a real risk but not disqualifying. The conceptual step of selection is most clearly Melitz's, and Helpman's extension to exporting versus FDI is the natural second name. A mechanism-centred citation and a full Scientific Background can handle the boundary. Some welfare magnitudes depend on parametric assumptions, but the qualitative mechanism is robust. P002 (Grossman and Helpman) is a close second because its attribution is cleaner and the framework is durable, although its empirical confirmation is mixed. I would not credit Helpman twice. P003 follows because of its breadth, offset by weaker identification, the 2024 institutions overlap and attribution across three names. P004 follows because of its credible designs but debated persistence and magnitudes and an unresolved task-framework and third-name attribution. Judged on merit, every proposal is better than no award, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: No profile-based tie to the laureates in P001 (Helpman, Melitz), P002 (Grossman, Helpman), P003 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) or P004 (Autor, Hanson, Dorn). Disclosed non-candidate ties: frequent co-author of committee secretary Krusell and co-author of chair Hassler, both of whom support P003, which I rank third, so their views are not independent evidence for me. Long-running collaboration with Klenow (credited on B036), Aghion, Bergeaud and Li, none of whom appears in any proposal in the slate. IIES and Stockholm ties are with committee colleagues, not candidates. Disclosed and not adjudicated.
